# Scan configuration

Keys under `scan` in `config/loom.php` decide which directories `loom:scan` walks. Publish the file to change them:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=loom-config
```

## Keys

<!-- generated:config-scan -->
<!-- Generated by `composer docs:generate`; edit the source, not this block. -->

| Key | Env variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.paths` | none | `['app']` | Directories loom:scan walks, relative to the project root. A `*` matches within one path segment (`Modules/*`). Paths outside the project root are rejected. Convention directories (Events, Listeners, Jobs, Mail, Notifications) resolve inside each one. |
| `scan.route_paths` | none | `['routes']` | Directories holding route files, relative to the project root. `*` globs are allowed (`Modules/*/routes`). Read for `routes[]` and for dispatches inside route closures; independent of `scan.paths`. |
| `scan.discover_routes` | none | `true` | Also read route files that Laravel loads from a statically resolvable path: `loadRoutesFrom()`, `Route::group()` with a file path and the `withRouting()` paths in bootstrap/app.php. `false` reads only `scan.route_paths`; `loom:scan --no-discover-routes` does the same for one run. |
| `scan.exclude` | none | `[]` | Globs relative to the project root. A match removes the file, or everything under the matching directory, from every scanner. |
<!-- /generated:config-scan -->

`loom:scan --path=DIR` replaces `scan.paths` for one run and `--route-path=DIR` replaces `scan.route_paths`; `scan.psr4_paths` and `scan.exclude` still apply. `--no-discover-routes` turns off route-file discovery for the run.

## How directories resolve

Convention directories (`Events/`, `Listeners/`, `Jobs/`, `Mail/`, `Notifications/`) are looked for directly under every entry of `scan.paths`. Everything else (dispatch sites, `$listen` arrays, observers, `Schedule::` calls, `Console/Kernel.php`) is found anywhere under a scan directory. Directories that don't exist are ignored; if none exist, `loom:scan` exits `1`.

| Layout | `scan.paths` |
| --- | --- |
| Default Laravel | `['app']` |
| `Modules/Billing/Events/...` | `['app', 'Modules/*']` |
| `Modules/Billing/app/Events/...` | `['app', 'Modules/*/app']` |
| `lib/Domain/Events/...` | `['lib/Domain']` |
| `Modules/Billing/routes/web.php` | nothing when a provider loads it with `loadRoutesFrom()`; otherwise `scan.route_paths`: `['routes', 'Modules/*/routes']` |

## Route files

Laravel loads a route file with `require`, from any path. Loom reads the files under `scan.route_paths` and, while `scan.discover_routes` is on, every file these calls load by a statically resolvable path:

| Call | Path argument |
| --- | --- |
| `$this->loadRoutesFrom($path)` in a service provider | `$path` |
| `Route::group($attributes, $path)` and `Route::...->group($path)` | `$path`, or an array of paths |
| `->withRouting(web:, api:, commands:)` in `bootstrap/app.php` | a path, or for `web` and `api` an array of paths |
| `->withCommands([...])` | file entries; directories are skipped |

Paths resolve when built from string literals, `.` concatenation, `__DIR__`, `DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR`, `dirname()`, `base_path()` and `app_path()` (assuming `app/`). A discovered file is searched for further loading calls. Loom looks for these calls in the files under `scan.paths`, the route files, `bootstrap/app.php`, and the providers in `bootstrap/providers.php` and `config/app.php`, so a module provider outside `scan.paths` is still found when the app registers it.

The final set is `scan.route_paths` plus discovered files, minus `scan.exclude`. A path that cannot be followed is counted in the summary line and listed by `loom:scan -v` with its file, line and reason: not statically resolvable (variable, method call, config value), relative to the working directory (`'routes/x.php'` with no `__DIR__` or `base_path()`), outside the project root, or no such file.

### Group attributes of the loading call

A loaded file's routes inherit the group around the loading call, as Laravel requires the file inside that group:

| Loading call | Applied to the file's routes |
| --- | --- |
| `Route::middleware('web')->prefix('shop')->name('shop.')->group($path)` | prefix `shop`, name prefix `shop.`, middleware `web` |
| `Route::group(['prefix' => 'x', 'as' => 'x.', 'middleware' => 'auth'], $path)` | the same three attributes |
| `$this->loadRoutesFrom($path)` inside a `Route::...->group(function () {...})` | the attributes of that group |
| `withRouting(web: $path)` | middleware `web` |
| `withRouting(api: $path)` | middleware `api` and prefix `api`, or the literal `apiPrefix:` |
| `Route::controller(C::class)->group($path)` | default controller for bare method-name actions |

`loadRoutesFrom()` on its own adds nothing, because Laravel does not wrap it in a group. Groups inside the loaded file nest inside the loading group, and a file that loads another passes the combined attributes on. A file loaded from two places is read once per loading group and can appear under two prefixes. Middleware is recorded by name, so `web` and `api` are not expanded; `domain`, `where` and `namespace` of the loading group are not recorded. An attribute that is not a literal (`->prefix($prefix)`, `->middleware($list)`) is not guessed: the file is still read and its routes carry the attributes that did resolve, and `-v` lists these under "Group attributes not applied". With `scan.discover_routes` off no loading call is followed, so no group is applied.

## Locating classes

When a dispatch names a class outside a convention directory, Loom finds its file through the PSR-4 map in `composer.json` (`autoload.psr-4`) as Composer does: longest matching prefix first, each directory in order, then the empty prefix. With no `composer.json` or no `psr-4` entry, `App\` is assumed to map to `app/`. A located file must be inside a scan directory and not excluded, otherwise the class is dropped.

## Exclude globs

| Pattern | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `app/Legacy` | The directory and everything under it |
| `app/*/Fakes/*.php` | One directory level between `app/` and `Fakes/` |
| `**/Fakes` | Any `Fakes` directory at any depth |
| `app/**/*.generated.php` | Generated files at any depth under `app/` |

`*` and `?` never cross a `/`; `**` does. Matching is case-sensitive. Excludes also apply to route files, `routes/console.php` and `bootstrap/app.php`.
